clue.text: At which fellows served rotten food?

parts.note: meat or game that is high has gone off, so rotten means high
table can mean the food provided, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: A diner wonders where the college dons were dished up spoiled food.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a question about a place: the raised table in a college hall at which the fellows dine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oxbridge colleges the dons, or fellows, eat at a raised dining table in hall set apart from the students.

clue.text: Courage demonstrated by resistance in passion

indicators.note: in means resistance goes inside the word for passion

parts.note: heat means passion or intensity, as in 'the heat of the moment'
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Bravery is shown by someone who fights back in the heat of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means courage or spirit, as in 'take heart' or 'lose heart'.

clue.text: Let slip drop vital catch, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to let slip is to reveal a secret accidentally
in cricket a fielder who drops a crucial catch may hand the match to the opponents

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, dropping a catch lets the batter survive, which can lose the match; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal a secret by accident, and literally to throw away victory in a contest.

clue.text: Unlucky for being abandoned — harsh

indicators.note: being abandoned says the word for is left out of the word for unlucky

parts.note: fortuneless means without fortune, unlucky

explanation.surface: An unlucky person, deserted by friends, finds life harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, discordant sound lacks melody, which is what being without a tune means.

clue.text: Improve on way sound vegetable's produced

indicators.note: sound says the words are said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: to improve on is to beat, and a way is a route, together 'beat route'

explanation.surface: Fixing a road with good acoustics yields a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat route' (improve on, way) said aloud gives the vegetable; ''s produced' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a red root vegetable, often pickled or roasted.

clue.text: European has to move swiftly over old currency

parts.note: to scud is to move fast, especially of clouds driven by wind
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A European must hurry across to a defunct currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a positional link, but it supplies O, the cricket abbreviation for an over.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro, so it is an old unit of money.

clue.text: Set up by Gordon, odd parts only

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the word up follows the picked letters
only the odd-numbered letters of Gordon are kept, the first, third and fifth

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Gordon puts together a set using only the odd parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A set and a group are both a collection of things or people classed together, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl admitting tennis shot's all over the place

indicators.note: admitting means the word for girl lets the shot inside it

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a lob is a high tennis shot; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A girl confesses that her tennis shot went wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' seems to describe the wayward shot, but it is the definition: worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means worldwide, found everywhere, which is being all over the place.

clue.text: Penguins aren't happy

parts.note: penguins live at the bottom of the globe in Antarctica, not at its peak, and the phrase for the peak means elated

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase means at the North Pole; penguins live in the far south, so they are not at that spot, and the idiom means elated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely happy and elated, as if standing at the summit of the globe.

clue.text: Workman repairs later crack, shutting out draught

indicators.note: crack signals that the letters are broken and rearranged
shutting out says certain letters are excluded from the jumble

parts.note: a draught is a current of air

explanation.surface: A tradesman fixes a crack later, keeping out the draught.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of REPAIRS LATER after removing AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer is a tradesman who applies plaster to walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Go on a trip round Venezuelan capital

indicators.note: round says the a-plus-trip pair wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in 'trip the light fantastic'

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of Venezuelan is wanted

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off on a tour around the capital of Venezuela.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venezuelan capital' suggests Caracas, but 'capital' only asks for the first letter, V, which goes inside A DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to move forward or proceed, which is what advancing means.

clue.text: Garment protecting king, one leading a country

indicators.note: one leading a means the I comes directly before the A
the garment protects the king by wrapping around it

parts.note: a coat is a garment
R is short for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A robe shields a king while somebody leads a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country in the Balkans on the Adriatic, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: It might be grand to keep lecture short

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut from the word for lecture

parts.note: a talk is a lecture

explanation.surface: A speaker hopes the talk will be impressive but brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as splendid, but a grand total is the sum of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand total is a kind of sum, so the word for a sum might be grand.

clue.text: Lecture given by communist which is laid down for the elite

definitions.text: which is laid down for the elite

indicators.note: given by means the lecture word follows the communist word

parts.note: red is a common informal word for a communist
to carpet someone is to reprimand them, give them a lecture

explanation.surface: A communist rails against privilege in a lecture about the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of crimson matting is rolled out for VIPs to walk on, so it is laid down for important guests.

clue.text: To boy one's introduced to, maintain serious dislike

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert

indicators.note: introduced to means the one goes into the word for boy

parts.note: a son is a boy
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A parent insists a son shows real distaste for someone he has met.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or repugnance, so serious dislike is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: A fast way to gain momentum crossing road in European city

indicators.note: crossing means the built word straddles the road abbreviation, holding it inside
to gain says the next piece is taken in by A plus the fast way

parts.note: steam is a fast way of travel, as in 'full steam ahead'
M is the symbol for momentum in physics

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a quick way to speed up while crossing a road in a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, a city in Europe.

clue.text: A service back in the Antipodes?

indicators.note: back means the word for the service is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a military service is returning from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Australia and New Zealand are a long way off from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are on the far side of the world from Britain, so being there means being far away.

clue.text: Suppose footballer's legal position to be in credit

indicators.note: to be in means the position sits inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a footballer who is onside is legally positioned and not offside

explanation.surface: A footballer wonders whether his legal standing puts him in the black.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to think about it or regard it as so, which is to suppose.

clue.text: Warning about happiness bypassing English

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: bypassing means leaving out the letter for English from the word for happiness

parts.note: delight is great happiness

explanation.surface: A caution is issued about joy that skips the English.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic signal of that colour warns to stop, and figuratively any danger signal is a warning.

clue.text: Criticise tricky accomplishment?

definitions.meaning: to criticise harshly in the press is to pan or knock
in bridge a grand achievement is winning all thirteen tricks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' means involving tricks: in bridge, winning every trick in a hand is a grand slam.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam is to criticise severely, and in bridge a slam is a contract winning all or all but one of the tricks.

clue.text: United achieving embarrassing score in tie

indicators.note: in means the score is put inside the word for tie

parts.note: to tether is to tie up an animal
OG, an own goal, is an embarrassing score in football

explanation.surface: A football side scores an own goal in a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, matching the score and tie, but it is the definition. OG is the standard football abbreviation for own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are united are joined as one, which is the sense of being together.

clue.text: Poor me — suit too small

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: too small means the word for suit is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to suit is to agree with, as in 'spicy food doesn't agree with me'

explanation.surface: Someone laments that their suit is too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' reads as clothing, but it is the verb: AGREE, cut short to AGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or deficient in quantity, which is poor in the sense of inadequate.

clue.text: A ringleader involved in fraud seeks religious retreat

indicators.note: involved in means the leader letter is placed inside the word for fraud

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or pretence
the leader, or first letter, of ring is R

explanation.surface: The leader of a fraud ring hides out in a religious retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious community or hermitage, a place of spiritual retreat.

clue.text: Break even in different schemes, finally

indicators.note: in means the word even sits inside the word for different

parts.note: else means other or different, as in 'someone else'
taken as written

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of schemes

explanation.surface: Someone tries to break even with a range of different schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break even' looks like a phrase, but 'Break' alone is the definition. ELEVENSES is a British mid-morning snack or tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light snack taken at about eleven in the morning, a short pause from work.

clue.text: Jersey perhaps here; where are trousers in relation?

definitions.meaning: a Jersey is a breed of cow, an animal that moos
trousers sit further down the body than a jersey, the woolly top

explanation.walkthrough: A Jersey is both a breed of cow and a knitted top; one that lows is a cow, and trousers are worn below the jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow lows, so it is a thing that lows; trousers are worn nearer the ground than a sweater, at a less high level.

clue.text: Device turning run out to runs

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
taken as written
R stands for runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer is run out going for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter or engine.

clue.text: Dignified woman having to carry out venture

parts.note: to do a task is to carry it out
to venture money on something is to wager it, to bet

explanation.surface: A stately lady takes on a risky undertaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically an elderly woman of stately bearing.

clue.text: Gentle pace wrong, being above all in the wrong direction

indicators.note: the whole run of letters is read the wrong way round, from back to front

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
God is the being above all others

explanation.surface: A slow walk is judged wrong, everything going the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is an easy, steady jog, a gentle running pace.

clue.text: Gone in the morning, travelling west —— east, possibly

indicators.note: in an across answer travelling west is going right to left, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: by means gone or past, as in 'days gone by'
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone who left in the morning heading west might have gone east instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Possibly and maybe both express that something could be so but is uncertain.

clue.text: Universal martyrdom virtually destroyed Catholic monarch

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: virtually means almost all of the word, here dropping the last letter

explanation.surface: Widespread martyrdom nearly ruined a Catholic queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' takes the last M off martyrdom to give MARTYRDO; add U and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary I of England, of the house of Tudor, was a Catholic queen who restored Catholicism in England.
